evidence: 0x40118a: lea rax, [rbp - 0x20] defines the destination 32-byte stack buffer
0x40118e/0x401191: rsi and rdi are set to argv[1] and the stack buffer, respectively
0x401194: call 0x401060 invokes strcpy@plt with no length limit
The proof-of-concept input of 32 or more bytes overwrites the saved frame and produces SIGSEGV

root_cause: handle copies attacker-controlled argv[1] into a 32-byte stack buffer using an unbounded strcpy, so input length >= 32 overwrites saved rbp/return address.

edits.reason: Redirect the vulnerable strcpy call site to the guard stub in the R-X segment tail.
Guard stub: compute argv[1] length, tail-call strcpy if <=31; otherwise write invalid_stderr to fd 2 and exit(1).
Exact invalid_stderr bytes written on the invalid path.

stub.source:
push rdi
mov rdi, rsi
xor eax, eax
mov rcx, -1
repne scasb
mov rax, -2
sub rax, rcx
pop rdi
cmp rax, 31
ja .error
jmp 0x401060
.error:
mov eax, 1
mov edi, 2
lea rsi, [rip + message]
mov edx, 42
syscall
mov eax, 60
mov edi, 1
syscall
message:
.byte 'ERROR: input exceeds destination capacity', 0x0a

valid_path: The stub computes the length of argv[1]. If the length is <=31, it restores the original destination pointer and tail-calls strcpy@plt (0x401060). strcpy writes the input plus NUL into the 32-byte buffer and returns to 0x401199. handle then calls puts, writing the input followed by a single LF to stdout; main returns 0.
invalid_path: If the length is >31, the stub branches to the error path. It uses write(2, invalid_stderr, 42) and exit(1) syscalls, never returning to handle. Therefore no strcpy or puts occurs, stdout remains empty, fd 2 receives exactly the 42 invalid_stderr bytes, and the process exits with status 1 without crashing.

stated_criteria_coverage.how: The guard allows at most 31 bytes before the terminating NUL, so strcpy writes at most 32 bytes into the destination buffer.
The guard compares the source length to 31 and treats lengths >31 as invalid.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_domain: printable ASCII, length 0..31, no NUL
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The guard only rejects based on length; argv[1] is a NUL-terminated C string, so valid-domain strings are handled correctly.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: valid_behavior: write input followed by LF to stdout; exit 0
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The valid path tail-calls the original strcpy and returns to the existing puts call; the original main return value of 0 is preserved.
The length check prevents strcpy from copying more than 31 bytes plus the terminator, so the saved frame is not overwritten.

stated_criteria_coverage.criterion: invalid_response: write exactly invalid_stderr to fd 2; exit 1; no stdout; no crash
stated_criteria_coverage.how: The error path uses raw write and exit syscalls to emit the exact 42 invalid_stderr bytes and terminate with status 1 without returning to handle.

assumptions: The bytes at 0x401211 and 0x401260 are within the existing R-X segment and are unused padding after .fini; they may be overwritten under allowed_edits.
Linux x86_64 syscall ABI is available; no new imports, PLT/GOT entries, or text relocations are needed.
argv[1] is a NUL-terminated C string; embedded NUL characters are not part of the valid domain.
The original valid-path return value is preserved because the stub tail-calls strcpy and does not alter the return address or callee-saved registers.
The execution environment permits syscall from the R-X segment.
uncertainties: The bytes currently at 0x401211 and 0x401260 are not shown in the disassembly; the plan assumes they are available padding and can be overwritten.
contract_sha256 and prompt_sha256 are not supplied; zero hashes are used as placeholders.
The verifier may expect a conventional libc exit rather than a raw exit syscall; the contract forbids new dynamic imports but does not forbid syscall.
The exact contents of the old bytes in the unused tail are not specified; an empty original_bytes indicates no known original bytes.
verification_proposal: Apply the three edits at the specified addresses without changing segment permissions or adding imports.
Run with argv[1] length 31 (31 printable ASCII): expect stdout exactly arg + LF, exit code 0, stderr empty.
Run with argv[1] length 32 (32 printable ASCII): expect exit code 1, stdout empty, stderr exactly the 42 invalid_stderr bytes, no SIGSEGV.
Run with the PoC 64 'A' bytes: expect exit code 1, no SIGSEGV, stderr exactly the invalid_stderr bytes, stdout empty.
Run with empty string: expect stdout LF only, exit 0.
Check that the handle valid path returns to 0x401199 and main returns 0.
